The scoring function also factors in the resulting position's material balance weighted by 10, and rewards moves that control central squares based on their distance from the board center. Finally, the function retrieves all legal moves and returns the one with the highest score, falling back to generating all possible moves if none are legal. Piece values are weighted (pawns at 100, knights and bishops at 320-330, rooks at 500, queens at 900) to properly evaluate capture opportunities. Pawn promotions receive heavy scoring (800+ points) since advancing to a queen dramatically shifts the game. Checks add tactical pressure with a 50-point bonus, while the overall material balance gets multiplied by 10 to ensure the AI recognizes when it's ahead or behind. Center squares are valued up to 20 points to encourage positional play beyond just material counting. The evaluation combines these factors to identify moves that either win immediately, gain material advantage, or improve board position—all within the computational constraints of a one-second decision window.
